searchText: I do prefer this on the beacon node as well, but I really like to avoid introducing another endpoint which cannot support ssz due to using an enum <@680234424037670912> based on your comment here https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/710831784991916072/1505695972045619200, you rather have it resolved by client, I think that was what Jim's v2 validators api proposal did? ah yes the whole point there was to remove `status` https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/449 builder endpoints (#610) https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/601 is not something we wanna consider? I feel like in general it would be nice to have an enum represenation in ssz so we are not blocked by such simple issues.. a long time ago I was thinking about adding `Enum` to the ssz spec, maybe should revive that effort i just don't think we need to be creating meta objects and v2 did a better job, but it depends on the data ppl are actually using which we have no metrics on. Generating 1GB of data from a BN is a sure-fire way to nuke it, i certainly dont think we should be encouraging fetching a 2 million item list in any format, but if we do have to then the standard validator structure is 'less bad' than doing computation to create a new meta object for 2 million entries. My preference if we're generating a meta object is to be severely restricting the scope and not allowing open ended responses of the entire data set 100% i think we need ssz support (imo for all endpoints) worst case, i think /validators being able to return the entire ssz straight off the state is 'less bad' if ppl really want the whole data set also i haven't measured the performance of this query since we were around 400k so im not sure how long the response would take now agree, would a generic enum ssz type be something we should consider? it seems like a gap in ssz to be a proper wire format a translation to enum im not strictly against, but the use case im dubious of given the sheer size of the data set its arguably less expensive to return a number does mean any consumer needs to be understanding that value, and also arguably is a breaking change if it was just ssz and we continue to return string in json, then its not breaking horrible to implement :/ but non breaking what you mean by number? enum is a number... if we broke the json it'd save MB it would just be a byte mapping, we just need a simple way to define that, ideally something generic but #601 would work to and shouldn't be breaking as it just affects ssz which we currently don't support if we're going to do this whole change to support ssz then its non trivial. id really like to understand why ppl are consuming it and if they really need all the data we're returning if we go down this road. given thats not going to happen though, we can add ssz support and clients can choose to implement it? i just dont like the shape of this endpoint at all its actually tempting to deprecate it and build what ppl need, but we dont know what ppl need ultimately so the pain is just how we wanna deal with `status` which was the main blocker on https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/449 as we didn't wanna drop it and same point raised by Potuz about builder endpoints here https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/710831784991916072/1509176030386983182, also I remember some discussion with rocketpool that they would prefer to have the `status` in the response for builders it is simpler, as you could just compute it on the client side by fetching the finalized checkpoint for example, if just status of specific validators is needed, then thats a very different shape to a complete exhaustive dump of validators its a lot of data to fetch if you're just looking for status from validator client point of view, we want the whole validator (or at least index) + status, ideally ssz encoded, the validator identities endpoint solves the minimal use case but not sure how I feel about introducing that whole set of endpoints for builders too, we could have an endpoint that just returns statuses but that seems ugly as well im not against the builder endpoints as a theory as long as we're not introducing tech debt like the get+post etc yeah that for sure not, but what about the custom object in Potuz's Pr with the `status`? also should not need a separate endpoint for balances, left another comment here https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/610#discussion_r3314209359 i need to look up how builder balances worked to answer that properly, i assumed they had effective and actual balances if they dont then sure - i defer to your judgement on that one at least by the state object shape it looks like a separate balance endpoint would not be required not sure if we'd need to have access to pending payments and withdrawals? ok - so - ssz support - implies support for status as enum - balance is built into builder object anyway - status is presumably a new set of rules, they have differing requirements compared to validators? withdrawal etc all dift i do prefer different endpoints to validators, just sounds like we need to not model builders on validators endpoints possibly, seems similar to `GET /eth/v1/beacon/states/{state_id}/pending_deposits`, and others we added to avoid fetching the whole state yeh i think as a model fetching all the high level lists from state as endpoints is nicer than fetching whole state if we're doing an encoding for status on builders, we could just use a number or soemthing rather than string builder status is simpler, should be pretty much just be `is_active_builder` in the spec ok great, so can just be boolean-ish if theres just that one extra attribute, do we need that as a filter? and if we're only returning active by default then theres not need to add it to the object... so the main thing would be - do we add a field - do we generate an array of statuses so there should be `pending`, `active` and `withdrawable`, a builder can't have an exited status as we have index reuse, so it will no longer exist/be overriden once fully exited does it become withdrawable instantly on exit? it appears that its active until its withdrawable so it'd be pending for like 2 epochs till finalized, then active until withdrawable epoch thats ok i can read up on that, just making sure i understand there is a long delay before funds are withdrawn, and index resue is determined by `get_index_for_new_builder` do we want to keep the builder object as it is in spec or add thestatus? could try to shape the output to keep the object 'the same', just not sure who prefers what. this was a point of contention with validators endpoint iirc i dont love changing the standard object but also dont love losely coupled data `[{builder: {}, status: 'XXX'}]`

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content:
i just don't think we need to be creating meta objects and v2 did a better job, but it depends on the data ppl are actually using which we have no metrics on.
Generating 1GB of data from a BN is a sure-fire way to nuke it, i certainly dont think we should be encouraging fetching a 2 million item list in any format, but if we do have to then the standard validator structure is 'less bad' than doing computation to create a new meta object for 2 million entries.

My preference if we're generating a meta object is to be severely restricting the scope and not allowing open ended responses of the entire data set
